summary: Alberta lookout in our records; no public source found names this tower or describes its build, staffing, fires or current state.

evidence.supports: Alberta's government publishes a map showing 127 wildfire lookout sites across the boreal forest and along the Rocky Mountains
evidence.quote: Map showing the locations of Alberta's 127 wildfire lookout sites, which are situated throughout the province's boreal forest and along the Rocky Mountains.

evidence.supports: each site is staffed by a lookout observer, generally from April to October, watching for wildfire all day
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

evidence.supports: in the boreal forest, steel was introduced for lookout towers in the 1920s and gradually displaced wood
evidence.quote: Introduced in the 1920s, steel increasingly replaced wood for tower construction.

evidence.supports: in 1945 lookouts began using the Osborne, an instrument for pinpointing where a fire lies relative to the tower
evidence.quote: Then in 1945, lookouts adopted the Osborne, an instrument used to help determine the precise location of a fire in relation to the tower.

evidence.supports: many of Alberta's operational lookouts are rebuilt on the spots where the first generation stood
evidence.quote: Many of Alberta’s 127 operational fire lookouts are rebuilt on the location of the first generation of lookouts.

notes_for_editor: PROTECTED DATA, LEFT OUT: the brief's 1962 build year, height (30 m), elevation, access ('closed') and staffing values come from the Alberta Wildfire WF_WILDFIRE_LOOKOUT layer, which its metadata marks as protected and not for public maps (same handling as Gift Lake). None appear in the story or facts; the story also avoids the 1960s cupola sentence from the Lonely Lookouts article, since a reader could take it as this tower's date. Decide before publishing them. NO SITE SOURCE: two searches found no public page naming this tower. Canada Lookouts has no Legend page (the URL I tried returns 404). firelookout.ca's Alberta view loads its rows by script, so the cache holds none. A local scan of cached web pages found no lookout mention of Legend. The 2009 Alberta NW-region lookout map text (data/raw/expansion/prairies-north/ab_lookout_map_2009.txt) does print LEGEND among lookout-site names near Ells River, but that cache has no public URL and the map is not quotable, so it is not cited. The name also matches many unrelated pages. The story is generic Alberta context plus an honest 'today' line, and it is a candidate to hold until a site-specific source turns up, as Gift Lake is. No photos found.
